questions.q: What does an identity provider (IdP) do?
options: It stores sharing rules for an org
It authenticates a principal and vouches for their identity to other systems
It only issues OAuth consumer secrets
It is another name for a Salesforce profile
questions.explain: The IdP owns the 'who are you' answer — it authenticates the user and then vouches for that identity to relying service providers.

questions.q: In a setup where employees log into Okta and then access Salesforce without logging in again, which role is Salesforce playing?
options: Identity provider (IdP)
Principal
Service provider (SP)
Credential issuer
questions.explain: Salesforce is relying on Okta's authentication decision, which makes Salesforce the service provider (SP) in that relationship.

questions.q: What is a 'principal' in identity terminology?
options: The administrator who configures Single Sign-On Settings
The entity being authenticated, such as a user or a system
The certificate exchanged between IdP and SP
A synonym for 'permission set'
questions.explain: The principal is whoever (or whatever) is being authenticated — usually a human user, but it can be a system or device acting on its own behalf.

questions.q: What does an SP validate when it receives a SAML assertion from an IdP?
options: The user's actual password
The assertion's signature against a trusted certificate, and that it hasn't expired
The user's permission set assignments
Nothing — assertions are accepted automatically
questions.explain: The SP cryptographically verifies the assertion's signature against a certificate it already trusts and checks the assertion hasn't expired, before establishing a session — no password is ever transmitted.

questions.q: Why can Salesforce legitimately act as both an IdP and an SP, sometimes in the same org?
options: Because profiles and permission sets change depending on the role
Because the underlying authorization model (profiles, permission sets, sharing) is unaffected by which identity role Salesforce is playing
Because Salesforce cannot actually do this — only one role is allowed per org
Because IdP and SP are the same thing with different names
questions.explain: Authentication and authorization are independent (Lesson 1). Which identity role Salesforce plays changes how a session gets established, not what that session is subsequently authorized to do.
